claim_summary: An LLM-driven feedback loop edits and evaluates anomaly-detector programs against synthetic held-out training-region anomalies, yielding compact univariate and multivariate spectral-Gaussian detectors.

claim_evidence.quote: model not as the detector but as the author of one: an autonomous research loop in which the model repeatedly edits a single short NumPy program under a leakage-free objective, keeping the bestscoring detector it finds.

modules.name: Detector-program edit-and-evaluate loop
modules.scope_reason: The core logic requires per-timestep anomaly-score output and selects edits by an anomaly-validation score; changing task family changes that output contract and objective, so it meets R3_1_TSK.

modules.name: Leakage-free synthetic-anomaly validation
modules.scope_reason: The verifier injects labelled synthetic anomalies and scores anomaly-detector outputs, so its validation criterion is bound to anomaly detection and would need redesign for another task family; R3_1_TSK therefore takes precedence.

evidence.quote: The search uses no real anomaly labels. Candidates are scored by detecting synthetic anomalies injected only into a held-out slice of each series’ training region.
The validation slice is the last 30% of each series’ training region (at least 128 steps); synthetic anomalies are injected only into this slice with a fixed seed.

modules.name: Univariate spectral-organization detector
modules.scope_reason: The contributed program directly computes anomaly scores for a univariate series using a task-specific novelty objective; changing task family changes the score output and procedure, so R3_1_TSK applies.

evidence.quote: Rather than looking at the raw values in a window, this detector looks at how the window’s energy is split between fast and slow rhythms, and at the overall shape of that split.
is scored by a shrunk full-covariance Mahalanobis distance to the Gaussian of normal windows and fused across a dyadic scale space with a tail-emphasized weighting.

modules.name: Multivariate joint band-power detector
modules.scope_reason: The contributed program computes multichannel anomaly scores from a joint spectral descriptor and anomaly novelty objective; changing task family changes the output contract and procedure, so R3_1_TSK applies.

evidence.quote: For series with many channels, the detector describes the rhythms of all channels together. It slides a window across the channels, removes each window’s level so that only its shape matters, and measures how much energy each channel carries in a few frequency bands.
It then builds a single statistical model of what normal windows look like and scores each window by how far it lies from that model.

task_performance.quote: The detector discovered by the Opus 4.8 loop takes the most first-place finishes on every one of the four metrics, and its advantage is widest on the precision-oriented metrics (standard F1 and VUS-PR).

notes: The paper also contributes two separately reusable Opus detector programs; ablation variants from the other searches are not counted as additional modules.
